matches.title: Implement long-press drag interaction with snap grid
matches.description:
Build the complete drag interaction pipeline: long-press activation on drag handles, pointer-capture-based drag movement, snap grid quantization, boundary clamping, position persistence on release, and visual feedback during drag.

## What to build

### Long-press recognizer (crates/tze_hud_input/src/)
Implement a LongPressRecognizer (or compositor-internal state machine — per RFC amendment decision in hud-bs2q.1):
- Threshold: configurable, default per device type. Check the RFC 0004 amendment from hud-bs2q.1 for the final timing decision (likely 200-300ms mouse, 1000ms touch).
- Movement tolerance: 10dp — moving pointer >10dp during hold cancels activation
- Progressive visual feedback: emit progress events (0.0→1.0) during hold for compositor to animate handle fill/pulse
- On success (hold completes without cancel): emit DragActivated internal event
- On failure (release or movement): reset state, no drag initiated
- Per-device independence: each device_id tracks its own long-press state

### Drag handler (crates/tze_hud_input/src/ or crates/tze_hud_compositor/src/)
On DragActivated:
- Acquire pointer capture for the device (runtime-internal chrome capture — see RFC 0004 amendment for timing rules)
- Record initial grab offset (pointer position relative to element's top-left)
- Begin tracking pointer moves: update element position to follow pointer with grab offset preserved

### Snap grid
- Quantize drag position to nearest grid point
- Grid density: configurable via design token drag.snap_grid_pct (default: 0.02 = 2% of display dimension, ~50x50 grid)
- Quantization formula: round(x_pct / snap_grid_pct) * snap_grid_pct

### Boundary clamping
- Constrain element to remain fully within display area during drag
- Clamp: x_pct >= 0.0, y_pct >= 0.0, x_pct + width_pct <= 1.0, y_pct + height_pct <= 1.0

### Position persistence on release
- On pointer release: release capture, compute final position (snap + clamp)
- Convert to GeometryPolicy::Relative { x_pct, y_pct, width_pct, height_pct }
- Persist to element store (atomic write)
- End movable state

### Visual feedback during drag (V1-COMPATIBLE — no shadows, no scale, no animated transitions)
Check what hud-bs2q.1 decided for v1-compatible visual effects. Expected:
- On drag start: temporary z-order boost (element renders above siblings), opacity increase, highlight border (2px)
- During drag: element follows pointer in real-time. Optional subtle snap grid overlay.
- On drag end: z-order returns to normal, border removed, element at new position

## Key files
- crates/tze_hud_input/src/lib.rs — InputProcessor, pointer event processing
- crates/tze_hud_input/src/capture.rs — pointer capture manager
- crates/tze_hud_input/src/events.rs — SceneLocalPatch, InputEnvelope
- crates/tze_hud_compositor/src/ — visual feedback rendering
- crates/tze_hud_scene/src/types.rs — GeometryPolicy::Relative (lines ~1421-1438)

## OpenSpec reference
- openspec/changes/persistent-movable-elements/specs/drag-to-reposition/spec.md — Requirements: 'Long-press activation for drag', 'Drag movement with pointer capture', 'Snap grid during drag', 'Position persistence as relative geometry', 'Movable state visual feedback', 'Boundary constraints during drag'

## Dependencies
- Requires hud-bs2q.1 (RFC amendments) for final gesture timing and visual effect decisions
- Requires hud-bs2q.2 (element store) for position persistence
- Requires hud-bs2q.3 (geometry override) for applying persisted positions
- Requires hud-bs2q.4 (drag handles) for HitRegion targets

## Tests
- Unit: long-press activation at threshold, cancellation before threshold, cancellation on movement
- Unit: multi-touch independence (per device_id)
- Unit: snap grid quantization accuracy
- Unit: boundary clamping at all four edges
- Integration: full drag flow (press handle → hold → drag → release → position persisted)
- Compositor: visual feedback during drag (z-boost, opacity, border)
matches.acceptance_criteria:
1. Long-press activates drag after configured threshold with 10dp tolerance
2. Progressive visual feedback during hold (0.0→1.0 progress)
3. Failed long-press (early release or movement) does not initiate drag
4. Pointer capture acquired on activation, element follows pointer with grab offset
5. Snap grid quantizes to nearest grid point (default 2%)
6. Boundary clamping prevents element from going off-screen
7. Position persisted as GeometryPolicy::Relative on release
8. Visual feedback uses v1-compatible effects only (z-boost, opacity, border — no shadows/scale/transitions)
9. Multi-touch: independent drag per device_id
10. All unit and integration tests pass
matches.notes:
V1 VISUAL EFFECTS CLARIFICATION:
- Progressive fill during long-press hold (0.0→1.0 progress): This is a state-driven value updated per-frame based on elapsed time. It is NOT an animated transition in the v1-deferred sense. Implement as: progress = min(1.0, elapsed_ms / threshold_ms), applied as a fill or opacity multiplier each frame.
- Lift effect on drag start: z-order boost (temporary +1000 to z_order) + opacity increase to 1.0 + 2px highlight border. NO drop shadows, NO scale pulses, NO ease-out transitions.
- Settle on drag end: z-order restored, border removed, element snaps to grid position INSTANTLY (no animated settle).

matches.title: Render chrome-layer drag handles on all elements
matches.description:
Add always-visible drag handles to every display element (zone, widget, tile) in the compositor's chrome layer. Handles are the entry point for all drag-to-reposition interaction.

## What to build

### Design tokens (crates/tze_hud_scene/src/types.rs or RenderingPolicy)
Add drag handle design tokens to RenderingPolicy or a dedicated DragHandleStyle struct:
- color: Rgba (default: semi-transparent white)
- opacity_idle: f32 (default: 0.4)
- opacity_active: f32 (default: 1.0)
- size_dp: (f32, f32) (default: 24.0 x 8.0 density-independent pixels)
- border_radius: f32
- grip_pattern: enum (Dots | Bar | None)

### Compositor rendering (crates/tze_hud_compositor/src/)
For each visible element (tile, zone with active content, widget with active publish), render a drag handle:
- Position: top-center of element bounds, slightly overlapping the element's top edge
- Layer: chrome (render above all content — use LayerAttachment::Chrome semantics)
- Visual: subtle grip dots or thin bar based on grip_pattern token
- Opacity: idle=0.4, transitions to 1.0 on hover (desktop) or press (mobile)
- Size: 24x8dp, scaling with display DPI

Important: only render handles on *visible* elements. Zones without active content and widgets without active publishes do not show handles.

### HitRegion for each handle (crates/tze_hud_input/ or crates/tze_hud_scene/)
Create a HitRegionNode per drag handle:
- accepts_pointer: true
- auto_capture: false (capture is acquired AFTER long-press succeeds, not on initial press)
- accepts_focus: false (drag handles should not participate in tab-cycling)
- interaction_id: 'drag-handle:<element_id_hex>' (for identifying which element is being dragged)
These are runtime-internal chrome HitRegions — NOT exposed over the wire protocol to agents.

### Opacity transition
Implement idle → active opacity transition:
- On hover (desktop) or press (mobile): transition opacity from idle (0.4) to active (1.0)
- On leave/release: transition back to idle
- Use RenderingPolicy transition timing (or a fixed 150ms ease-in-out)

### Handle on passthrough tiles
Passthrough tiles (input_mode: Passthrough) still get drag handles because handles are chrome-layer. Chrome always wins hit-testing per RFC 0001 §5.2.
Note for overlay mode: drag handles create 24x8dp input dead zones on passthrough elements. This is documented as an acceptable trade-off for discoverability.

## Key files

matches.title: Amend v1.md and RFCs for movable elements
matches.description:
Before any implementation can begin, 5 conflicts found during doctrine/RFC reconciliation must be resolved by amending the relevant documents.

## Context
Three independent reconciliation passes (doctrine, RFC, consistency) found that the persistent-movable-elements design conflicts with existing v1 scope boundaries and RFC contracts. These are spec/doc amendments, not code changes.

## What to amend

### 1. v1.md persistence scope (about/heart-and-soul/v1.md)
Current text (line ~145): 'No scene persistence across display node restarts (tab/layout config, auth registrations, and runtime widget/SVG asset store do persist).'
Amendment: Add 'element identity store (user geometry overrides and element metadata)' to the carve-out list.
Rationale: The element store is user-owned layout preferences (like config), not agent scene content.

### 2. RFC 0004 gesture promotion (about/legends-and-lore/rfcs/0004-input.md)
LongPress and Drag are currently V1-reserved (§3.2, ~line 70). The drag handle interaction needs both.
Two options (pick one):
a) Promote LongPress and Drag to V1-mandatory, scoped to chrome-layer drag handles only. Document that the full gesture arbiter (§3.3-§3.6) is NOT required — drag handles use a compositor-internal state machine.
b) Add a note that chrome-layer interactions may implement gesture-like behaviors outside the V1-reserved gesture pipeline.
Also: Amend §2.2 to clarify that the capture-on-PointerDown constraint applies to agent-requested capture; runtime chrome interactions may acquire capture at any event phase.
Also: Either adopt the 500ms LongPress threshold from §3.4 or explicitly amend it to 1000ms for drag handles, with rationale that 1s reduces false activations on mobile touch targets. Consider device-discriminated delay (200-300ms for mouse, 1000ms for touch) since v1 is desktop-only.

### 3. Replace v1-deferred visual effects in OpenSpec specs
File: openspec/changes/persistent-movable-elements/specs/drag-to-reposition/spec.md
The 'Movable state visual feedback' requirement (lines ~128-136) mandates drop shadows, scale pulses (1.02x), and ease-out transitions — all explicitly deferred in v1 (architecture.md line ~141).
Replace with v1-compatible feedback: z-order boost, opacity change (e.g., 0.8→1.0), 2px highlight border. Remove all references to drop shadows, scale pulses, and animated transitions.

### 4. Define mobile reset gesture
File: openspec/changes/persistent-movable-elements/specs/drag-to-reposition/spec.md
Current 'Reset via long-press on mobile' scenario (lines ~89-91) is unimplementable: same 1s long-press gesture activates both drag and reset context menu.
Replace with a concrete, implementable gesture. Recommended: short tap on drag handle shows a small 'Reset' button (3-second auto-dismiss). This avoids gesture conflict entirely.

### 5. Define PublishToTileMutation semantics
Files: openspec/changes/persistent-movable-elements/specs/element-identity-store/spec.md, about/legends-and-lore/rfcs/0001-scene-contract.md
- Clarify relationship to existing SetTileRootMutation (coexist: PublishToTile for element-store addressing, SetTileRoot for raw tile_id)
- Specify that lease validation applies (agent needs active lease on tile's namespace)
- Allocate proto field number in SceneMutation oneof (next available after existing 9 variants)
- Add 'Runtime Override Application' stage to RFC 0001 §3.2 transaction pipeline (between Validate and Commit) for applying user geometry overrides
- Also: Add DragHandle to ChromeElement enum in RFC 0001
- Also: Correct factual error — ZoneDefinition already has 'pub id: SceneId' (types.rs:1551). The change makes these IDs persistent, not assigns them.
- Also: Add element store to RFC 0001's durability model (§6.1 or equivalent)

## Acceptance
1. v1.md carve-out list includes element identity store
2. RFC 0004 documents gesture promotion or compositor-internal mechanism
3. RFC 0004 §2.2 clarifies capture timing for runtime chrome interactions
4. OpenSpec drag-to-reposition spec uses only v1-compatible visual effects (no shadows, no scale, no animated transitions)
5. Mobile reset gesture is concretely defined with no ambiguity
6. PublishToTileMutation has defined semantics, field numbers, and lease validation rules
7. RFC 0001 has DragHandle in ChromeElement enum, element store in durability model, and runtime override application stage in transaction pipeline
8. ZoneDefinition SceneId factual error corrected in proposal.md and design.md

matches.title: Persistent movable elements
matches.description:
Add drag-and-drop repositioning of all display elements (zones, widgets, tiles) with persistent position overrides. The display runtime owns durable element identity, exposes discovery APIs, and persists user-chosen positions across sessions.

## Motivation
Users cannot customize the spatial layout of their display. Positions are set by agents (tiles) or config defaults (zones/widgets). This contradicts 'screen is sovereign' doctrine. Users — not agents — should decide where things live.

## Scope
- Persistent element identity for ALL element types (zones, widgets, tiles)
- Element discovery API (gRPC ListElements + MCP list_elements)
- Publish-to-element-by-ID for element reuse across sessions
- Always-visible drag handles (chrome layer, floating-window style)
- 1-second long-press activation, fine-grained snap grid, percentage-based persistence
- Reset-to-default position (right-click/context menu)
- Agent notification (ElementRepositionedEvent, notification only — cannot reject)
- User can move ANY element including agent tiles (screen is sovereign)

## OpenSpec Change
All artifacts at openspec/changes/persistent-movable-elements/:
- proposal.md — motivation, what changes, capabilities
- design.md — 7 decisions (D1-D7) with rationale
- specs/element-identity-store/spec.md — 7 requirements, 17 scenarios
- specs/drag-to-reposition/spec.md — 9 requirements, 23 scenarios
- tasks.md — 13 task groups, 52 tasks

## Reconciliation Findings (must resolve before implementation)
Three doctrine/RFC reconciliation passes found 5 conflicts:
1. LongPress/Drag are V1-reserved in RFC 0004 — need promotion or compositor-internal bypass
2. Drop shadows/transitions are v1-deferred — need v1-compatible replacement
3. v1.md says 'no scene persistence' — need element store carve-out
4. Mobile reset gesture is ambiguous — need distinct gesture from drag activation
5. PublishToTileMutation undefined in RFC 0001 — need semantics, field numbers, lease validation

## Key Architecture
- Element store: %LOCALAPPDATA%/tze_hud/element_store.toml (persist forever, no GC)
- Geometry override resolution: user drag > agent bounds > config override > default policy
- All overrides stored as GeometryPolicy::Relative (percentage-based, resolution-independent)
- Drag handles: chrome-layer HitRegions, always capture input, 24x8dp

## Affected Crates
tze_hud_scene, tze_hud_input, tze_hud_compositor, tze_hud_protocol, tze_hud_runtime, tze_hud_config, MCP bridge

5. Agent receives ElementRepositionedEvent notification (cannot reject)
6. Reset-to-default clears user override, falls through to next resolution tier
7. Fine-grained snap grid during drag, boundary clamping to display area
8. All spec scenarios in element-identity-store and drag-to-reposition pass

matches.title: TimingHints and presentation scheduling
matches.description:
Sub-bead #2 of Epic 3 (Timing Model). Implement TimingHints struct, presentation scheduling, expiration enforcement, timestamp validation, pending queue, staleness indicators, message class enum, clock drift detection/enforcement, freeze/safe-mode timing behavior, headless virtual clock, ClockSync RPC, and timing configuration.

Parent epic: rig-zyeo (Epic 3: Timing Model)
Depends on: sub-bead #1 (rig-voo8, clock domain types)

## Spec requirements (v1-mandatory)

### Requirement: Timing Fields on Payloads (spec lines 72-83)
All meaningful realtime payloads MUST carry timing fields: present_at_wall_us (or relative scheduling alternative), expires_at_wall_us, created_at_wall_us, sequence, priority, coalesce_key, sync_group. The oneof schedule fields MUST be mutually exclusive; setting more than one MUST be rejected with RELATIVE_SCHEDULE_CONFLICT.

WHEN/THEN scenarios:
- WHEN an agent submits a MutationBatch, THEN it MAY set present_at_wall_us, expires_at_wall_us, sequence, priority, coalesce_key, sync_group; compositor MUST interpret and enforce each (spec lines 77-79)
- WHEN an agent sets both present_at_wall_us and after_us in the same message, THEN compositor MUST reject with RELATIVE_SCHEDULE_CONFLICT (spec lines 81-83)

### Requirement: Timestamp Precedence (spec lines 85-92)
present_at_wall_us MUST follow precedence: node-level overrides tile-level, tile-level overrides batch-level.

WHEN/THEN scenarios:
- WHEN a TextMarkdownNode has present_at_wall_us = T1 and its parent tile has T2, THEN the node MUST use T1 (spec lines 90-92)

### Requirement: Frame Quantization (spec lines 94-105)
present_at_wall_us timestamp T is "in scope" for frame F iff T <= frame_F_vsync_wall_us. Strict no-earlier-than rule.

WHEN/THEN scenarios:
- WHEN a mutation has present_at_wall_us = V + 1ms (where V is vsync time of frame F), THEN it MUST NOT apply at frame F; MUST wait until frame F+1 (spec lines 99-101)
- WHEN a mutation has present_at_wall_us = T, THEN it MUST be applied no earlier than T and no later than T + one frame period (spec lines 103-105)

### Requirement: Arrival Time Is Not Presentation Time (spec lines 50-61)
Every payload with timing significance MUST carry explicit timestamp fields. Mutations with present_at_wall_us in the future MUST be held in pending queue. Mutations without present_at_wall_us (or = 0) SHALL be applied at earliest available frame.

WHEN/THEN scenarios:
- WHEN agent submits MutationBatch with present_at_wall_us = T+500ms, THEN compositor MUST store and NOT apply until vsync_wall_us >= T+500ms (spec lines 55-57)
- WHEN agent submits with present_at_wall_us = 0, THEN apply at earliest available frame (spec lines 59-61)

### Requirement: Timestamp Validation (spec lines 107-122)
Validation rules for all agent-supplied timestamps:
- present_at_wall_us > 60s in past -> TIMESTAMP_TOO_OLD
- present_at_wall_us > max_future_schedule_us (default 300,000,000us = 5min) in future -> TIMESTAMP_TOO_FUTURE
- expires_at_wall_us <= present_at_wall_us -> TIMESTAMP_EXPIRY_BEFORE_PRESENT
- DROP_IF_LATE with non-EPHEMERAL_REALTIME class -> INVALID_DELIVERY_POLICY
- clock skew > 1s -> CLOCK_SKEW_EXCESSIVE

WHEN/THEN scenarios:
- WHEN present_at_wall_us > 60s before session_open_wall_us, THEN reject with TIMESTAMP_TOO_OLD (spec lines 112-114)
- WHEN present_at_wall_us > 5min in future, THEN reject with TIMESTAMP_TOO_FUTURE (spec lines 116-118)
- WHEN expires_at_wall_us <= present_at_wall_us, THEN reject with TIMESTAMP_EXPIRY_BEFORE_PRESENT (spec lines 120-122)

### Requirement: Presentation Deadline (spec lines 236-251)
Mutations held in per-agent pending queue (sorted by present_at_wall_us ascending, max depth 256 per agent). Late arrivals deferred to next frame. EphemeralRealtime with DROP_IF_LATE MAY be dropped.

WHEN/THEN scenarios:
- WHEN frame's vsync_wall_us >= mutation's present_at_wall_us, THEN extract from pending queue to Stage 4 (spec lines 241-243)
- WHEN pending queue has 256 entries, THEN reject new with PENDING_QUEUE_FULL (spec lines 245-247)
- WHEN EPHEMERAL_REALTIME with DROP_IF_LATE arrives after Stage 3 closes, THEN discard (spec lines 249-251)

### Requirement: Expiration Policy (spec lines 253-268)
Tile with expires_at_wall_us = T auto-removed at first frame where vsync_wall_us >= T. Min-heap O(expired_items). Non-negotiable under load (even degradation Level 4/5). Expiring tile removed from sync group before deletion.

WHEN/THEN scenarios:
- WHEN tile's expires_at_wall_us reached, THEN remove from scene at Stage 4, emit TileExpired event (spec lines 258-260)
- WHEN compositor at degradation Level 5, THEN expiry still runs (spec lines 262-264)
- WHEN 1000 tiles exist but only 2 expired, THEN evaluation touches only 2 (spec lines 266-268)

### Requirement: Session Close Pending Queue Flush (spec lines 291-298)
All entries in closed session's pending queue MUST be discarded. Reconnecting agent starts with empty queue.

WHEN/THEN scenarios:
- WHEN session closes with 10 pending mutations, THEN all 10 discarded, MUST NOT apply after reconnect (spec lines 296-298)

### Requirement: Staleness Indicators (spec lines 300-311)
Two staleness conditions: content staleness (no mutation within tile_stale_threshold_ms default 5000ms) and sync group staleness (arrival spread exceeds sync_drift_budget_us). Chrome-layer visual badge. Cleared on new valid mutation or agent disconnect.

WHEN/THEN scenarios:
- WHEN STATE_STREAM tile receives no mutation for 5s, THEN activate staleness badge (spec lines 305-307)
- WHEN stale tile receives new valid mutation, THEN clear staleness immediately (spec lines 309-311)

### Requirement: Message Class Typed Enum (spec lines 369-380)
Four message classes as typed MessageClass enum: Transactional, StateStream, EphemeralRealtime, ClockedMediaCue. Each has distinct delivery semantics.

WHEN/THEN scenarios:
- WHEN agent submits EPHEMERAL_REALTIME with DROP_IF_LATE, THEN accept (spec lines 374-376)
- WHEN agent submits DROP_IF_LATE with TRANSACTIONAL, THEN reject with INVALID_DELIVERY_POLICY (spec lines 378-380)

### Requirement: Vsync Sync Point (spec lines 32-39)
At each frame start, record (frame_number, vsync_mono_us, vsync_wall_us). Include in TelemetryRecord.

WHEN/THEN scenarios:
- WHEN new frame begins at vsync, THEN record sync point triple in FrameTimingRecord (spec lines 37-39)

### Requirement: Session Clock Sync Point (spec lines 41-48)
During gRPC handshake, record session_open_mono_us and session_open_wall_us. Difference is initial clock-skew estimate.

WHEN/THEN scenarios:
- WHEN agent establishes gRPC session, THEN record both timestamps and compute initial clock-skew estimate (spec lines 46-48)

### Requirement: Clock Drift Detection and Correction (spec lines 210-221)
Sliding window of last 32 agent timestamps for clock-skew estimation (median). Drift within tolerance (<=100ms): apply signed offset correction transparently. Clock jump (consecutive samples differ by > clock_jump_detection_ms default 50ms): reset window.

WHEN/THEN scenarios:
- WHEN agent clock is 50ms ahead, THEN apply -50ms correction transparently (spec lines 215-217)
- WHEN consecutive skew samples differ by > 50ms, THEN reset estimation window (spec lines 219-221)

### Requirement: Clock Drift Enforcement (spec lines 223-234)
Drift > 100ms: CLOCK_SKEW_HIGH warning, continue with correction. Drift > 1s: reject with CLOCK_SKEW_EXCESSIVE. Three consecutive ClockSync failures: terminate session.

WHEN/THEN scenarios:
- WHEN drift is 200ms, THEN emit CLOCK_SKEW_HIGH warning, continue with correction (spec lines 228-230)
- WHEN drift exceeds 1s, THEN reject new mutations with CLOCK_SKEW_EXCESSIVE (spec lines 232-234)

### Requirement: ClockSync RPC (spec lines 382-389)
Unary RPC for agents to align clocks. Request: agent_timestamp_wall_us. Response: compositor_mono_us, compositor_wall_us, estimated_skew_us, skew_within_tolerance, warning.

WHEN/THEN scenarios:
- WHEN agent calls ClockSync after session establishment, THEN compositor returns current timestamps and estimated skew (spec lines 387-389)

### Requirement: Freeze Override Timing Behavior (spec lines 326-341)
During freeze: pending queue drain suspended, expiry heap suspended, sync group deferred_frames_count not incremented, staleness timer suspended, clock-skew estimation continues. On unfreeze: apply past-due mutations, expire past-due tiles, resume staleness from pre-freeze, drop past-due DROP_IF_LATE ephemeral.

WHEN/THEN scenarios:
- WHEN scene frozen and tile's expires_at_wall_us passes, THEN NOT expired during freeze; expired in first post-unfreeze Stage 4 (spec lines 331-333)
- WHEN tile idle 4800ms and 2s freeze occurs, THEN not stale until 200ms after unfreeze (spec lines 335-337)
- WHEN scene unfreezes and mutations have present_at_wall_us in past, THEN all applied in first post-unfreeze Stage 3/4 (spec lines 339-341)

### Requirement: Safe Mode Timing Behavior (spec lines 343-358)
During safe mode: pending queue drain runs normally, expiry runs normally, staleness suppressed for suspended sessions, clock-skew estimation frozen. On exit: estimation window reset, staleness timers reset to 0.

WHEN/THEN scenarios:
- WHEN safe mode active and tile's expires_at_wall_us reached, THEN tile expired on schedule (spec lines 349-351)
- WHEN safe mode active and suspended session's tile has no mutations, THEN staleness NOT shown (spec lines 353-355)
- WHEN safe mode exits, THEN clock-skew estimation window reset to empty (spec lines 357-358)

### Requirement: Headless Virtual Clock (spec lines 360-367)
In headless mode, configurable frame rate (default 60fps) driven by synthetic clock. Same pipeline and timing semantics.

WHEN/THEN scenarios:
- WHEN compositor runs headless, THEN all timing behavior identical to windowed mode (spec lines 365-367)

### Requirement: Timing Configuration (spec lines 391-402)
All timing parameters configurable via TimingConfig with defaults and validation ranges: target_fps (60, 1-240), max_agent_clock_drift_ms (100, 1-10000), max_vsync_jitter_ms (2, 0-100), max_future_schedule_us (300000000, 1000000-3600000000), sync_group_max_defer_frames (3, 1-60), pending_queue_depth_per_agent (256, 16-4096), sync_drift_budget_us (500, 1-100000), tile_stale_threshold_ms (5000, 500-300000), clock_jump_detection_ms (50, 10-10000).

WHEN/THEN scenarios:
- WHEN config sets target_fps = 0, THEN runtime MUST reject (outside range 1-240) (spec lines 396-398)
- WHEN no [timing] section in config, THEN use all documented defaults (spec lines 400-402)

## Crate/file location
- crates/tze_hud_scene/src/timing/ (new module: hints.rs, scheduling.rs, pending_queue.rs, expiration.rs, staleness.rs, config.rs)
- crates/tze_hud_scene/src/clock.rs (extend for vsync sync point, clock drift)
- Proto definitions for TimingHints, MessageClass enum, ClockSync RPC

## Relevant test scenes
- lease_expiry — expiration behavior
- coalesced_dashboard — state-stream coalescing with coalesce_key
- chatty_dashboard_touch — ephemeral realtime with DROP_IF_LATE

## Cross-epic contracts
- Session-protocol (Epic 6) consumes ClockSync RPC, session clock sync point, session close queue flush
- Input-model (Epic 5) uses TimingHints for input event timestamps

## Acceptance criteria

- Presentation scheduling: future mutations held, immediate mutations applied
- Timestamp validation: TIMESTAMP_TOO_OLD, TIMESTAMP_TOO_FUTURE, TIMESTAMP_EXPIRY_BEFORE_PRESENT, CLOCK_SKEW_EXCESSIVE all produce structured errors
- Frame quantization: no-earlier-than guarantee verified with TestClock
- Pending queue: sorted, max depth 256, PENDING_QUEUE_FULL rejection
- Expiration: min-heap, O(expired_items), non-negotiable under degradation
- Staleness indicators: 5s threshold, cleared on mutation
- Clock drift: sliding window, median estimation, jump detection, enforcement tiers
- Freeze/safe-mode: correct suspension/resumption semantics
- Headless mode: synthetic clock drives same pipeline
- TimingConfig: all defaults, all validation ranges, rejection of out-of-range values
- All tested with SimulatedClock for deterministic behavior

## v1-mandatory
All requirements listed above.

## v1-reserved exclusions
- None

- ClockedMediaCue active processing (spec lines 413-420) — enum value defined but not processed

matches.title: TTL, renewal, and expiration — lease lifecycle timing
matches.description:
Implement lease lifecycle timing per lease-governance/spec.md Requirement: Auto-Renewal Policy (lines 71-91), Requirement: Safe Mode Suspends Leases (lines 92-99), Requirement: Safe Mode Resume (lines 105-108), Requirement: Max Suspension Time (lines 114-122), Requirement: Suspension Preserves State (lines 123-131), and Requirement: TTL Accounting Precision (lines 289-296).

## Auto-Renewal Policies (spec lines 71-91, Requirement: Auto-Renewal Policy)
Three renewal policies:
- MANUAL (default): agent must explicitly send LeaseRequest with operation = RENEW before TTL expires
- AUTO_RENEW: runtime auto-renews at 75% TTL elapsed if session is Active and no budget violations pending; agent receives LeaseResponse with result = GRANTED on each auto-renewal
- ONE_SHOT: expires at TTL without renewal option; agent must request a new lease

Auto-renewal disabled (timer not armed) when:
1. Agent enters budget warning state (resumes if warning clears before TTL expires)
2. Session enters Disconnecting state
3. Safe mode is entered (TTL clock paused; timer resumes with TTL clock on safe mode exit)

ONE_SHOT leases: not subject to auto-renewal, but TTL clock IS paused during suspension.

## Safe Mode Suspends Leases (spec lines 92-99, Requirement: Safe Mode Suspends Leases)
On safe mode entry:
- All ACTIVE leases transition to SUSPENDED (NOT REVOKED)
- Agent sessions receive SessionSuspended with reason = "viewer_safe_mode"
- LeaseSuspend sent for each lease
- Mutations rejected with SAFE_MODE_ACTIVE
- TTL clock paused
- Auto-renewal suspended
- Suspension completes within 1 frame (16.6ms)

## Safe Mode Resume (spec lines 105-108, Requirement: Safe Mode Resume)
On safe mode exit:
- All SUSPENDED leases transition back to ACTIVE
- Agents receive SessionResumed
- LeaseResume sent with adjusted_expires_at_wall_us and suspension_duration_us
- Staleness badges clear within 1 frame
- Tiles render from last-committed scene state
- Resume completes within 2 frames (33.2ms)
- Agent does NOT re-request a lease

## Max Suspension Time (spec lines 114-122, Requirement: Max Suspension Time)
A lease MUST NOT remain SUSPENDED indefinitely. After max_suspension_time_ms (default: 300,000ms / 5 minutes), lease transitions to REVOKED. If safe mode remains active beyond this duration, suspended leases are progressively revoked (oldest first).

## Suspension Preserves State (spec lines 123-131, Requirement: Suspension Preserves State)
When suspended: all tiles, node trees, zone publications, resource allocations, and lease metadata preserved in memory. No resources freed.

## TTL Accounting Precision (spec lines 289-296, Requirement: TTL Accounting Precision)
TTL accounting during suspension accurate to +/- 100ms. Effective lease expiry: granted_at_wall_us + (ttl_ms * 1000) + suspension_duration_us.

## WHEN/THEN Scenarios from Spec

Scenario: Auto-renewal at 75% TTL (spec lines 76-78)
- WHEN a lease with AUTO_RENEW policy reaches 75% of its TTL
- THEN the runtime automatically renews the lease and sends LeaseResponse with result = GRANTED

Scenario: Auto-renewal disabled during budget warning (spec lines 80-82)
- WHEN a lease with AUTO_RENEW policy enters budget warning state
- THEN the auto-renewal timer is disarmed; the lease continues aging toward expiry and the agent must renew manually or resolve the budget warning before TTL elapses

Scenario: ONE_SHOT lease expires (spec lines 84-86)
- WHEN a ONE_SHOT lease reaches its TTL
- THEN the lease transitions to EXPIRED without renewal option

Scenario: ONE_SHOT lease suspended during safe mode (spec lines 88-91)
- WHEN a ONE_SHOT lease is active when safe mode is entered
- THEN the TTL clock pauses during suspension; on safe mode exit the lease transitions back to ACTIVE with adjusted expiry and can serve its full remaining TTL

Scenario: Safe mode suspends all leases (spec lines 97-99)
- WHEN the viewer triggers safe mode
- THEN all ACTIVE leases transition to SUSPENDED within one frame, agents receive SessionSuspended, and mutations are rejected

Scenario: TTL paused during suspension (spec lines 101-103)
- WHEN a lease is SUSPENDED for 2 minutes and then resumed
- THEN the effective TTL does not count the 2 minutes of suspension time

Scenario: Resume preserves lease identity (spec lines 110-112)
- WHEN safe mode is exited
- THEN all previously SUSPENDED leases return to ACTIVE with the same LeaseId, capability scope, and budget

Scenario: Suspension timeout (spec lines 119-121)
- WHEN a lease is SUSPENDED for more than 5 minutes (default)

matches.description:
Implement the core lease state machine per lease-governance/spec.md Requirement: Lease State Machine (lines 10-26) and Requirement: Lease Identity (lines 28-34).

## States
REQUESTED, ACTIVE, SUSPENDED, ORPHANED, REVOKED, EXPIRED, DENIED, RELEASED

## Valid Transitions (spec line 11)
- REQUESTED->ACTIVE (granted)
- REQUESTED->DENIED (denied)
- ACTIVE->SUSPENDED (safe mode)
- ACTIVE->ORPHANED (disconnect)
- ACTIVE->EXPIRED (TTL elapsed)
- ACTIVE->REVOKED (viewer dismiss, budget policy)
- ACTIVE->RELEASED (agent releases)
- SUSPENDED->ACTIVE (safe mode exit)
- SUSPENDED->REVOKED (max suspension time exceeded)
- ORPHANED->ACTIVE (reconnect within grace)
- ORPHANED->EXPIRED (grace period elapsed)
Terminal states: DENIED, REVOKED, EXPIRED, RELEASED — no further transitions possible.

## Lease Identity (spec lines 28-34, Requirement: Lease Identity)
Each lease carries: LeaseId (UUIDv7, time-ordered, SceneId type), namespace (agent identity string), session_id (parent session), granted_at_wall_us (UTC microseconds), ttl_ms (0 = indefinite), renewal_policy, capability_scope, resource_budget, lease_priority.

## Operations Requiring a Lease (spec lines 37-46, Requirement: Operations Requiring a Lease)
CreateTile, InsertNode, ReplaceNode, RemoveNode, UpdateTileBounds, UpdateTileExpiry MUST require an ACTIVE lease. Guest MCP ZonePublish MUST NOT require a lease. CreateTab, RemoveTab, read operations MUST NOT require a lease.

## Wire Protocol Integration (spec lines 307-314, Requirement: Wire Protocol Integration)
Lease messages flow over primary session stream within SessionMessage envelope:
- LeaseRequest (client->server): field 21
- LeaseResponse (server->client): field 31
- LeaseSuspend: field 47, LeaseResume: field 48, LeaseStateChange: field 49

## Lease Caps (spec lines 298-305, Requirement: Lease Caps)
Max 64 leases per runtime (all agents), max 8 default (64 hard max) per session, max 64 tiles per lease, max 64 nodes per tile.

## Each transition produces an auditable event.

## WHEN/THEN Scenarios from Spec

Scenario: Lease granted (spec lines 15-17)
- WHEN an agent sends a LeaseRequest with valid capabilities and budget within limits
- THEN the lease transitions from REQUESTED to ACTIVE and the agent receives LeaseResponse with result = GRANTED

Scenario: Lease denied (spec lines 19-21)
- WHEN an agent sends a LeaseRequest requesting capabilities beyond its session grants
- THEN the lease transitions to DENIED and the agent receives LeaseResponse with result = DENIED and populated deny_reason

Scenario: Invalid transition rejected (spec lines 23-25)
- WHEN a lease is in EXPIRED state
- THEN no further transitions are possible (terminal state)

Scenario: Lease identity fields populated (spec lines 32-34)
- WHEN a lease is granted
- THEN the LeaseResponse includes a UUIDv7 LeaseId, the granted TTL, priority, budget, and expiry timestamp

Scenario: Tile mutation without active lease (spec lines 41-43)
- WHEN an agent attempts InsertNode but its lease is in SUSPENDED state
- THEN the mutation is rejected with SAFE_MODE_ACTIVE error

Scenario: Guest zone publish without lease (spec lines 45-46)
- WHEN a guest agent publishes to a zone via MCP ZonePublishToken
- THEN the publish succeeds without requiring a lease

Scenario: Runtime-wide lease limit (spec lines 303-305)
- WHEN 64 leases are active across all agents and a new lease is requested
- THEN the request is denied with MAX_RUNTIME_LEASES_EXCEEDED

Scenario: Lease messages on session stream (spec lines 312-314)
- WHEN an agent sends a LeaseRequest
- THEN it is carried as field 21 of the SessionMessage oneof on the existing session stream

Scenario: Sub-millisecond lease grant (spec lines 248-251, Requirement: Lease Grant Latency)
- WHEN an agent sends a valid LeaseRequest
- THEN the LeaseResponse with result = GRANTED is emitted within 1ms

matches.title: Trait contract test harnesses for 5 v1 subsystems
matches.description:
Define Rust traits encoding spec requirements for 5 core subsystems, with companion test suites written against the trait. Any correct implementation must satisfy the tests. Tests compile but fail (or are #[ignore]d) until implementation lands.

## Spec Links

- lease-governance/spec.md lines 10-25: state machine (REQUESTED→ACTIVE→SUSPENDED/ORPHANED/EXPIRED/REVOKED/RELEASED/DENIED)
- lease-governance/spec.md lines 71-90: auto-renewal semantics (MANUAL, AUTO_RENEW at 75% TTL, ONE_SHOT)
- lease-governance/spec.md lines 92-104: safe mode (ACTIVE→SUSPENDED, TTL paused, resume ≤2 frames)
- lease-governance/spec.md lines 114-122: max suspension time (300,000ms default, revoke oldest-first)
- lease-governance/spec.md lines 132-155: orphan grace period (30,000ms, detection via heartbeat timeout 3×5000ms=15,000ms)
- lease-governance/spec.md lines 169-185: budget soft/hard limits (80%/100%)
- lease-governance/spec.md lines 187-200: three-tier budget enforcement ladder (Warning at 80%, Throttle at 85-95%, Revocation at 100% hard limit)
- policy-arbitration/spec.md lines 10-17: seven-level stack (Human Override → Safety → Privacy → Security → Attention → Resource → Content)
- policy-arbitration/spec.md lines 91-104: Level 2 Privacy Evaluation (VisibilityClassification vs ViewerClass redaction matrix)
- policy-arbitration/spec.md lines 143-166: attention budget (20/min per-agent, 10/min per-zone)
- policy-arbitration/spec.md lines 194-199: per-frame evaluation order and <200µs budget
- scene-events/spec.md lines 5-16: three-category taxonomy (Input, Scene, System)
- scene-events/spec.md lines 35-46: event type naming convention (scene.<object>.<action>)
- scene-events/spec.md lines 50-65: interruption classes (CRITICAL > HIGH > NORMAL > LOW > SILENT)
- scene-events/spec.md lines 92-103: quiet hours queue (FIFO per-zone, LatestWins coalesce, max 100)
- scene-events/spec.md lines 107-122: agent event emission (capability check, 4KB limit, 10 events/sec rate limit)
- scene-events/spec.md lines 156-183: subscription categories and capability mapping
- resource-store/spec.md lines 5-16: BLAKE3 content-addressed identity
- resource-store/spec.md lines 20-27: resource immutability
- resource-store/spec.md lines 31-42: v1 types (IMAGE_RGBA8, IMAGE_PNG, IMAGE_JPEG, FONT_TTF, FONT_OTF)
- resource-store/spec.md lines 57-68: chunked upload protocol
- resource-store/spec.md lines 72-79: small resource fast path (≤64KB inline)
- resource-store/spec.md lines 102-113: deduplication (hash hit → <100µs)
- resource-store/spec.md lines 117-124: concurrent upload limit (≤4 in-flight)
- resource-store/spec.md lines 128-147: reference counting semantics
- configuration/spec.md lines 10-21: TOML format, parse error line/column
- configuration/spec.md lines 23-34: file resolution chain (CLI → env → cwd → XDG)
- configuration/spec.md lines 36-47: minimal config requirements
- configuration/spec.md lines 49-82: built-in profiles (full-display, headless, mobile rejection)
- configuration/spec.md lines 84-99: profile auto-detection
- configuration/spec.md lines 101-112: budget escalation prevention
- configuration/spec.md lines 149-150: capability vocabulary (canonical wire-format names)

## Traits to Define

### 1. LeaseStateMachine
Encode lease lifecycle from lease-governance/spec.md:
- States: REQUESTED, ACTIVE, SUSPENDED, ORPHANED, EXPIRED, REVOKED, RELEASED, DENIED
- Methods: request(), activate(), suspend(), resume(), orphan(), expire(), revoke(), release(), deny()
- Queries: state(), ttl_remaining(), is_terminal(), can_transition_to()
- Clock injection via TestClock for TTL/grace period testing
- Budget enforcement thresholds: Warning at 80%, Throttle at 85-95%, Revocation at 100% hard limit (lease-governance/spec.md lines 187-200)

### 2. PolicyEvaluator
Encode policy-arbitration/spec.md:
- Input: typed PolicyContext (safety state, privacy classifications, capabilities, attention counters, resource budgets, zone contention)
- Output: PolicyDecision with applied_level, action, reason
- Must evaluate levels in order (0→6), short-circuit on first decisive result
- Level 2 (Privacy): VisibilityClassification vs ViewerClass redaction matrix (policy-arbitration/spec.md lines 91-104)
- Budget check: total evaluation <200µs (policy-arbitration/spec.md lines 194-199)
- Attention budget tracking: per-agent 20/min, per-zone 10/min

### 3. EventRouter
Encode scene-events/spec.md:
- Methods: emit(), subscribe(), unsubscribe(), enter_quiet_hours(), exit_quiet_hours()
- Event type validation: naming convention enforcement (scene.<object>.<action>)
- Interruption classification: route by class, enforce quiet hours rules
- Subscription filtering: category→capability mapping per lines 156-183
- Rate limiting: 10 events/sec per agent, 4KB payload limit

### 4. ResourceStore
Encode resource-store/spec.md:
- Methods: upload_start(), upload_chunk(), upload_complete(), upload_inline(), get(), delete(), gc()
- Content addressing: BLAKE3 hash identity
- Deduplication: hash hit returns existing, was_deduplicated=true
- Type validation: reject non-v1 types
- Concurrent limit: ≤4 in-flight uploads
- Reference counting: increment on node creation, decrement on deletion

### 5. ConfigLoader
Encode configuration/spec.md:
- Methods: parse(), normalize(), validate(), freeze()
- File resolution: ordered chain with first-found semantics
- Profile resolution: full-display, headless, mobile (rejected), auto-detection
- Budget escalation prevention: custom cannot exceed base values
- Capability vocabulary validation: reject unknown capability names
- Includes rejection: v1 does not support config includes

## WHEN/THEN Scenarios (representative subset)

LeaseStateMachine:
- WHEN lease is REQUESTED and activate() called THEN state becomes ACTIVE
- WHEN lease is ACTIVE and TTL elapses THEN state becomes EXPIRED
- WHEN lease is ACTIVE and safe mode entered THEN state becomes SUSPENDED, TTL paused
- WHEN lease is SUSPENDED and safe mode exits THEN state becomes ACTIVE within 2 frames (33.2ms), TTL resumes with adjusted expiry
- WHEN lease is SUSPENDED for >300,000ms THEN state becomes REVOKED (oldest-first)
- WHEN lease is ORPHANED and agent reconnects within 30,000ms THEN state becomes ACTIVE
- WHEN lease is ORPHANED and grace period elapses THEN state becomes EXPIRED
- WHEN lease is EXPIRED/REVOKED/RELEASED/DENIED and any transition attempted THEN error (terminal states)
- WHEN ONE_SHOT lease is SUSPENDED THEN TTL paused; on resume, adjusted expiry = original_expiry + suspension_duration
- WHEN budget at 80% THEN BudgetWarning emitted, mutations still accepted (Warning tier)
- WHEN budget at 85-95% THEN mutation rate throttled (Throttle tier)
- WHEN budget at 100% THEN MutationBatch rejected atomically with BUDGET_EXCEEDED (Revocation tier)

PolicyEvaluator:
- WHEN safety event (GPU failure) fires THEN Level 1 short-circuits, lower levels skipped
- WHEN privacy redaction required THEN Level 2 applied before security/attention/resource checks (policy-arbitration/spec.md lines 91-104)
- WHEN capability check fails THEN Level 3 returns CAPABILITY_REQUIRED within <5µs
- WHEN attention budget at 80% THEN AttentionBudgetWarningEvent emitted
- WHEN attention budget at 100% THEN mutations coalesced (latest-wins within agent+zone)
- WHEN total evaluation exceeds 200µs THEN budget violation logged

EventRouter:
- WHEN event emitted during quiet hours with class=NORMAL THEN queued in FIFO
- WHEN event emitted during quiet hours with class=LOW THEN discarded
- WHEN event emitted during quiet hours with class=CRITICAL THEN delivered immediately
- WHEN quiet hours exit THEN queued events delivered in FIFO order
- WHEN LatestWins zone in quiet hours receives 2 publishes THEN only latest kept in queue
- WHEN agent emits event without required capability THEN rejected
- WHEN agent exceeds 10 events/sec THEN rate limited

ResourceStore:
- WHEN identical bytes uploaded twice THEN same ResourceId returned, was_deduplicated=true, latency <100µs
- WHEN non-v1 type uploaded THEN rejected with TYPE_NOT_SUPPORTED
- WHEN 5th concurrent upload attempted THEN rejected with RESOURCE_TOO_MANY_UPLOADS
- WHEN chunked upload completes with hash mismatch THEN rejected
- WHEN resource refcount reaches 0 THEN eligible for GC

ConfigLoader:
- WHEN TOML has syntax error THEN parse error includes line and column
- WHEN profile=mobile THEN rejected with CONFIG_MOBILE_PROFILE_NOT_EXERCISED
- WHEN custom profile exceeds base budget THEN rejected with BUDGET_ESCALATION
- WHEN unknown capability in agent config THEN rejected with UNKNOWN_CAPABILITY
- WHEN config includes used THEN rejected (v1 does not support includes)

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] 5 Rust traits defined in dedicated modules
- [ ] Each trait has ≥10 #[test] functions encoding spec WHEN/THEN scenarios
- [ ] Tests use TestClock for all time-dependent assertions
- [ ] Tests compile against the trait (not a concrete type) — use generic test functions
- [ ] Tests fail or are #[ignore]d until correct implementation provided
- [ ] Total: ≥50 test functions across all 5 trait modules
- [ ] No implementation code — traits define the contract only

## Crate/File Locations

- LeaseStateMachine: crates/tze_hud_scene/src/lease/mod.rs (new module) + tests in crates/tze_hud_scene/src/lease/tests.rs
- PolicyEvaluator: crates/tze_hud_scene/src/policy/mod.rs + tests
- EventRouter: crates/tze_hud_scene/src/events/mod.rs + tests (or crates/tze_hud_protocol/src/events/)
- ResourceStore: crates/tze_hud_scene/src/resource/mod.rs + tests
- ConfigLoader: crates/tze_hud_scene/src/config/mod.rs + tests (or new crate crates/tze_hud_config/)

## What This Does NOT Include

This bead produces TRAIT DEFINITIONS AND TEST HARNESSES only. It does NOT:
- Implement the traits (that is implementation work for later beads)
- Add wire protocol tests (that is bead #4)
- Add pixel/rendering tests (that is bead #5)
- Modify existing runtime or compositor code

matches.title: Write Input RFC: focus, gestures, IME, accessibility, local feedback, hit-region primitives
matches.description:
Write the Input RFC — the interaction model specification for tze_hud. This RFC defines how user input (pointer, touch, keyboard, accessibility) flows through the system, how local feedback is guaranteed, and how the interactive hit-region node primitive works.

## Doctrine References (heart-and-soul/)

- **presence.md §Interaction** — Two-way interaction mandatory. Supports: touch, pointer, buttons, keyboard/mouse, voice triggers, sensor-initiated interrupts, app-to-agent callbacks. Local-first: pressed state, focus ring, visual ack happen locally and instantly.
- **presence.md §Focus model** — Per-tile, not per-agent. At most one tile has keyboard focus. Runtime manages focus transitions. Focus is local-first: visual indicator updates before agent notification.
- **presence.md §Input routing and bubbling** — Route through scene graph: chrome layer (always wins) → tiles in z-order (highest first) → nodes within tile. Unhandled events bubble: node → tile → tab → runtime.
- **presence.md §Gesture arbitration** — Runtime arbitrates cross-tile gestures. Default: tile where gesture started owns it.
- **presence.md §IME, text input, and accessibility** — First-class, not afterthought. Runtime exposes a11y metadata via platform APIs. Agents declare semantic roles. Runtime bridges to platform.
- **architecture.md §Window model** — Overlay mode: selective click-through. Interactive regions capture input; non-interactive pass through. Per-region determination follows scene graph.
- **v1.md §Interaction** — Mouse/pointer, touch, local-first feedback (press states, focus rings, hover highlights). Input events forwarded to owning agent. At least one retained interactive primitive: hit_region node with local pressed/hovered state, focus semantics, agent callback on activation.
- **validation.md §Split latency budgets** — input_to_local_ack p99 < 4ms.
- **failure.md §What the user always sees** — Screen responsive to touch/input within 4ms. Tab switching works. Safe mode override works.

## Required Sections

### 1. Input Event Model
- Raw event types from winit: PointerMoved, PointerPressed, PointerReleased, KeyPressed, KeyReleased, TouchStart, TouchMove, TouchEnd, Scroll, IMECommit, IMEPreedit
- Normalized internal event: InputEvent { kind, position (logical coords), timestamp (system mono), modifiers, device_id, touch_id (for multi-touch) }
- Coordinate spaces: physical pixels → logical pixels (DPI-scaled) → scene coords → tile-local coords → node-local coords
- Event timestamps: system monotonic at OS event receipt, not at processing time

### 2. Hit-Testing Pipeline
- Depends on Scene Contract RFC for spatial query definition
- Pipeline: raw position → scene coords → chrome layer hit test → z-ordered tile hit test → node hit test within tile
- Chrome always wins: runtime UI elements always capture input regardless of agent content
- Overlay mode passthrough: non-interactive regions return HitResult::Passthrough, which the window manager translates to click-through (WM_NCHITTEST HTTRANSPARENT / hitTest nil / XShape mask)
- Dynamic hit-test mask: updated every frame based on active tiles with input affordances. Cached as a bitmask for fast lookup.
- Performance: < 100μs per hit test (from Scene Contract), amortized across frame for hover tracking

### 3. Focus Model
- Focus state: FocusState { focused_tile: Option<TileId>, focused_node: Option<NodeId> }
- Focus transitions: pointer click → focus tile under pointer. Tab key → cycle focusable tiles. Agent cannot forcibly steal focus.
- Focus semantics: focused tile receives keyboard events. Non-focused tiles do not. 
- Visual feedback: focus ring rendered by compositor (chrome layer, not agent-controlled). Style: configurable, default 2px accent-color ring.
- Focus events to agents: FocusGained { tile_id, node_id }, FocusLost { tile_id, node_id } — delivered via agent session stream
- Programmatic focus request: agent can request focus for its own tile (granted if policy allows, never if another tile is mid-interaction)

### 4. Local Feedback Contract
- **THE critical latency path.** input_to_local_ack p99 < 4ms.
- Local feedback is rendered by the compositor, not by the agent. The agent is NOT in the feedback loop for:
  - Hover highlight: tile/node gains subtle highlight when pointer enters bounds
  - Press state: hit_region node visually depresses on pointer-down, releases on pointer-up
  - Focus ring: visual ring appears on focused tile/node
  - Scroll feedback: scroll position updates immediately
- These are compositor-side state machines driven by input events. The agent receives events *after* local feedback is already rendered.
- Implementation: local feedback state is part of the scene graph (per-node: hovered: bool, pressed: bool, focused: bool). Updated in the "local feedback" frame stage (stage 2 in Runtime Kernel RFC) with zero network roundtrip.

### 5. Gesture Model
- Gesture recognition: pointer/touch sequences classified into gestures
  - Tap: down + up within 300ms and 10px movement threshold
  - Long-press: down held > 500ms without movement
  - Drag: down + move beyond 10px threshold
  - Scroll: two-finger or scroll wheel
  - Pinch: two-touch with changing distance (multi-touch only)
  - Swipe: fast directional movement (velocity > 500px/s)
- Gesture ownership: the tile/node where the gesture *starts* (first pointer-down) owns the entire gesture sequence
- Cross-tile gesture arbitration: if a drag starts in tile A and moves to tile B, tile A owns it. Tile B does not receive events for that gesture.
- Gesture cancellation: if the owning tile is deleted or its lease is revoked mid-gesture, the gesture is cancelled and remaining events are discarded
- Gesture events to agents: GestureStart, GestureUpdate, GestureEnd, GestureCancelled — with gesture type, position, velocity, accumulated delta

### 6. Interactive Node Primitives (hit_region)
- V1 ships one retained interactive primitive: hit_region
- hit_region node properties:
  - bounds: Rect (within parent tile)
  - cursor: CursorType (pointer, hand, text, crosshair, etc.)
  - focusable: bool
  - a11y_role: AccessibilityRole (button, link, checkbox, slider, etc.)
  - a11y_label: String
  - enabled: bool (disabled regions show dimmed, don't capture input)
  - local_feedback_style: FeedbackStyle (default, custom colors, none)
- hit_region local state (compositor-managed):
  - hovered: bool (pointer within bounds)
  - pressed: bool (pointer down within bounds)
  - focused: bool (has keyboard focus)
- hit_region agent callbacks:
  - Activated (tap/click completed)
  - PressStart, PressEnd
  - HoverEnter, HoverExit
  - FocusGained, FocusLost
  - KeyEvent (when focused)

### 7. IME and Text Input
- IME lifecycle: StartComposition → PreeditUpdate(text, cursor) → CommitText(final) → EndComposition
- Platform IME integration: winit handles OS-level IME. Runtime bridges events to focused tile's agent.
- Preedit rendering: compositor renders preedit text at the focused node's position (agent does not render preedit)
- CJK, emoji, dictation: all handled through platform IME path
- Text input nodes: future extension. V1 hit_region receives key events; full text editing is deferred.

### 8. Accessibility
- Platform APIs: UI Automation (Windows), NSAccessibility (macOS), AT-SPI (Linux)
- Scene graph → a11y tree mapping: each tile → a11y container, each hit_region → a11y element with role + label
- Focus tracking: a11y focus follows compositor focus
- Screen reader narration: tile names, node labels, state changes (pressed, disabled, checked) announced
- Keyboard navigation: Tab cycles focusable elements, Enter/Space activates, Escape dismisses/unfocuses
- Minimum commitment: v1 exposes the a11y tree with correct roles, labels, and focus. Advanced patterns (live regions, custom actions, drag-and-drop a11y) deferred.

### 9. Protobuf Schema
- input.proto: InputEvent, HitResult, GestureEvent, FocusEvent, IMEEvent, AccessibilityNode
- Agent session stream carries: input events for owned tiles, gesture events, focus events, IME events

## Quantitative Requirements

- Hit-test latency: < 100μs per point query (50-tile scene)
- Local feedback latency (input_to_local_ack): p99 < 4ms
- Focus transition: < 1ms from input event to focus ring update
- Gesture classification: < 2ms from qualifying event to gesture event emission
- A11y tree update: < 5ms after scene commit
- IME preedit render: < 1 frame (16.6ms) from OS event to preedit visible
- Hit-test mask update: < 500μs per frame (for overlay click-through)

## Diagrams Required

Use /excalidraw-diagram to create:
1. Input routing pipeline: OS event → winit → local feedback → hit-test → agent event
2. Focus state machine: unfocused → focused (pointer/tab) → focused (agent request) → unfocused (pointer away/tab/revoked)
3. Gesture lifecycle: down → classify → own → update → end/cancel
4. hit_region node state machine: idle → hovered → pressed → activated → idle
5. Overlay click-through: scene graph → hit-test mask → platform pass-through

## Platform Targets

- Input: winit (cross-platform pointer, keyboard, touch, IME)
- A11y: accesskit (Rust, bridges to all three platform APIs)
- Overlay click-through: WM_NCHITTEST (Win), hitTest (macOS), XShape (X11), wlr-layer-shell (Wayland)
- Multi-touch: supported on touch-capable displays and mobile (winit touch events)

matches.title: Write E2E integration tests for movable elements
matches.description:
Write end-to-end integration tests that validate the full persistent-movable-elements feature across session boundaries, agent reconnection, and display changes. These tests exercise the complete pipeline from element creation through drag interaction to position persistence and reuse.

## What to test

### Test 1: Cross-session persistence
Agent creates tile → user drags tile to new position → runtime restarts → agent reconnects → tile appears at user-overridden position (not agent-requested bounds).
Validates: element store persistence, startup loading, geometry override resolution.

### Test 2: Element discovery and reuse
Agent creates tile (gets SceneId back) → disconnects → reconnects → calls ListElements(namespace filter) → finds previous tile → calls PublishToTile(element_id) → user override preserved.
Validates: ListElements API, PublishToTileMutation, override persistence across publish.

### Test 3: Reset fallback chain
User drags element → user resets position → element returns to agent-requested bounds (not some other position).
Validates: reset removes override, correct fallback tier.

### Test 4: Zone with config override
Zone has config-level geometry_override → user drags zone → user resets → zone returns to config override (NOT default geometry policy).
Validates: three-tier resolution for zones (user > config > default), reset falls to tier 2 not tier 4.

### Test 5: Display resolution change
User drags element to center of 1920x1080 display (x_pct=0.5, y_pct=0.5) → display changes to 3840x2160 → element renders at (1920, 1080) — still center.
Validates: percentage-based persistence survives resolution changes.

### Test 6: Agent notification
Agent creates tile → user drags tile → agent receives ElementRepositionedEvent with correct old_geometry and new_geometry.
Validates: event emission, correct geometry values, Transactional delivery.

## Test infrastructure
Use the existing headless Layer 0-1 test infrastructure (no GPU, no winit). See tests/integration/ for existing patterns (e.g., dashboard_tile_input.rs for input integration test patterns).

- tests/integration/ — existing integration test directory
- crates/tze_hud_input/src/hit_test.rs — headless hit-testing
- crates/tze_hud_scene/src/graph.rs — SceneGraph for test scene construction

- openspec/changes/persistent-movable-elements/specs/drag-to-reposition/spec.md — All scenarios

matches.title: Add reset-to-default and agent notification
matches.description:
Implement the reset-to-default-position feature and the ElementRepositionedEvent agent notification. These are the two remaining interaction features after the core drag pipeline.

## What to build

### Reset to default position (crates/tze_hud_input/, crates/tze_hud_compositor/)
Implement the reset gesture as defined in the RFC amendment from hud-bs2q.1 (which resolves the mobile gesture ambiguity). Expected approach: short tap on drag handle shows a small 'Reset' button or similar.

On reset activation:
- Remove geometry_override from element store entry for this element
- Re-resolve element geometry via fallback chain (agent bounds or config override or default policy)
- Animate element to new position (v1-compatible: opacity transition or instant snap)
- No-op if element has no user override

Right-click on desktop: show context menu with 'Reset to default position' option.
Context menu rendering: minimal chrome-layer popup (dismiss on click outside, 3-second auto-dismiss).

### Agent notification (crates/tze_hud_protocol/, crates/tze_hud_scene/)
Define ElementRepositionedEvent protobuf message:
- element_id: bytes (SceneId, 16 bytes LE)
- new_geometry: GeometryPolicyProto
- previous_geometry: GeometryPolicyProto
Message class: Transactional (reliable, ordered — must not be dropped under backpressure).

Allocate field number in SessionMessage oneof (server → client direction, next available).
Subscription category: scene_topology (natural fit with other scene change events).

Emit on drag completion (after position persisted to store):
- If agent is connected with active lease: deliver event on session stream
- If agent is disconnected or lease not active: skip delivery (override is persisted regardless)
- Agent cannot reject — no response mechanism

Also emit on reset-to-default (with new_geometry = the fallback position).

### Lease state edge cases
- User CAN reposition elements with SUSPENDED or ORPHANED leases (drag is a chrome-layer runtime operation, not an agent mutation)
- ElementRepositionedEvent only sent to agents with ACTIVE leases
- Override persists regardless of lease state

## Key files
- crates/tze_hud_input/src/ — gesture handling for reset
- crates/tze_hud_compositor/src/ — context menu rendering
- crates/tze_hud_protocol/proto/types.proto — GeometryPolicyProto
- crates/tze_hud_protocol/proto/events.proto — event definitions, SessionMessage oneof
- crates/tze_hud_scene/src/graph.rs — SceneGraph event emission

## OpenSpec reference
- openspec/changes/persistent-movable-elements/specs/drag-to-reposition/spec.md — Requirements: 'Reset to default position', 'Agent notification on reposition'
- openspec/changes/persistent-movable-elements/specs/element-identity-store/spec.md — Requirement: 'Geometry override resolution order' (reset clears tier 1, falls to tier 2/3/4)

## Dependencies
- Requires hud-bs2q.4 (drag handles) for handle interaction targets
- Requires hud-bs2q.5 (drag interaction) for the drag pipeline integration
- Requires hud-bs2q.3 (geometry override) for fallback chain after reset

## Tests
- Integration: reset removes override, element returns to agent bounds
- Integration: reset falls through to config override (not default) when config override exists
- Integration: reset on element without override is no-op
- Integration: agent receives ElementRepositionedEvent with old and new geometry
- Integration: disconnected agent does not receive event but override persists
- Integration: user can drag element with SUSPENDED lease

matches.title: RFC 0003: Define timer behavior during freeze and safe mode
matches.description:
## Problem

RFC 0007 (System Shell) defines two override states that affect the timing model but are not addressed by RFC 0003:

1. **Freeze (RFC 0007 Section 4.3):** Agent mutations are queued but not applied. The display shows the frozen scene. On unfreeze, queued mutations are applied in submission order.

2. **Safe mode (RFC 0007 Section 5):** All agent sessions receive SessionSuspended. Mutations are rejected with SAFE_MODE_ACTIVE until safe mode exits. On exit, pending mutations from the queue are applied.

RFC 0003 does not specify what happens to timing-sensitive state during these overrides:

- **present_at_us during freeze:** If a mutation has present_at_us = T and the scene is frozen at time T-1, does the mutation expire unused? Is T re-evaluated on unfreeze? The pending queue logic in Section 5.3 assumes normal frame progression.

- **expires_at_us during freeze:** If a tile has expires_at_us = T and the scene freezes at T-1, the expiry heap check (Section 5.4) would remove the tile on the next frame after T — but the tile's visual removal was deferred by freeze. Does the tile disappear instantly on unfreeze, or does freeze pause expiry evaluation?

- **Sync group deferral counters during freeze:** If an AllOrDefer group is mid-deferral when freeze activates, do the deferred_frames_count continue incrementing? If so, the group could force-commit while invisible, producing a state the viewer never saw.

- **Staleness indicators during freeze:** The tile_stale_threshold_ms timer (Section 4.7) would fire during freeze since mutations are queued, not applied. Should staleness indicators be suppressed during freeze?

- **Safe mode and session clocks:** During safe mode, sessions are suspended. Should the clock-skew estimation window (Section 4.3) be paused? Timestamps from a long safe mode period would skew the sliding window.

## Affected Sections

- Section 4.7 (Staleness Indicators) — needs freeze/safe-mode exception
- Section 5.3 (Presentation Deadline) — needs freeze behavior spec
- Section 5.4 (Expiration Policy) — needs freeze behavior spec
- Section 2.4 (Timing Contract) — needs freeze behavior for sync group deferral
- Section 4.3 (Drift Detection) — needs safe mode behavior for estimation window
- New subsection needed: 'Override State Interaction' or similar

## Doctrine Reference

architecture.md Section Policy arbitration: Human override always wins (position 1). RFC 0007 Section 4.5: Override effects appear within one frame. The timing model must not produce incorrect or surprising behavior when overrides are active.

## Concrete Change

Add a new section (e.g., Section 5.6 or a new top-level Section after Section 5) specifying:

1. **Freeze pauses timing evaluation.** present_at and expires_at evaluation is suspended during freeze. Expiry heap is not drained. Sync group deferral counters are paused. Staleness timers are paused. On unfreeze, timing resumes from the current wall clock — mutations whose present_at has passed are applied immediately; tiles whose expires_at has passed are expired immediately.

2. **Safe mode pauses per-session timing.** Clock-skew estimation window is frozen during SessionSuspended. On SessionResumed, the window is reset (not resumed with stale samples). Tiles with expires_at continue to be evaluated (safe mode does not prevent tile cleanup).

3. **Headless mode virtual clock.** Briefly note that headless mode with SimulatedClock does not have freeze/safe-mode concerns since the clock is manually advanced. But tests should cover freeze-then-advance-clock scenarios.

## Rationale

Freeze and safe mode are defined in the RFC set. The timing model must account for them or risk undefined behavior during override states.
